title: Quiz — a letter from London to India
subtopic: 3 — Calais: why this route exists (Quiz C)
learning_goal: Know why a train to the heel of Italy counted as a short cut to India.

narration.script: Calais, in the middle of the night. Before we board — one question about the train we are about to catch. Before any of this existed, how long did a letter from London take to reach India?
narration.after_script: Three months, round the Cape of Good Hope. A question and its answer took half a year. That is why a train to the heel of Italy counts as a short cut.

interaction.prompt: Before any of this existed, how long did a letter from London take to reach India?

options.feedback: Not yet. Three weeks is roughly what it took after everything in this chapter had been built — the railways, the canal, the steamers.

That was the new way, and it was a marvel. In the 1830s Thomas Waghorn pieced together a route through Egypt — ship, river, camels and carriages across the desert, ship again — and got it down to about six weeks.
Round the Cape of Good Hope: over eleven thousand miles, and about three months each way.
